subject: Post-call: deployment mode & cost framework for pilot
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme-corp.com>, Procurement <procure@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment mode & cost framework for pilot

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Recap here so we have a shared starting point and clear asks for next week.

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Primary goal: ship a customer-facing summarization feature for internal ops by Q3 with strict 200ms median latency target and 95th percentile < 400ms for short prompts.
- Expected steady-state: ~40 RPS (reads) during business hours with 3x peak bursts (so ~120 RPS infrequently).
- Typical prompt sizes: 120-300 tokens input + 100-400 tokens output; estimated avg tokens per request ~420.
- Data residency: US-only. No on-prem required for pilot; private VPC considered for production if approved by security.

Deployment options we discussed (high-level economics):
1) Hosted API: fast to production, pay-as-you-go per-token. Ballpark for pilot (based on your usage profile): ~0.4–0.7 USD per 1k tokens depending on model family and streaming. For 40 RPS steady with ~420 tokens per req, rough hosted cost = ~40 * 420 * 3600 * 10 * 0.0005/day — we included an example workbook attached to show how this scales.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): better unit economics at scale and predictable monthly commit. Typical pilot recommendation: 1–2 reserved GPU workers with autoscale buffer if you target latency SLOs, with a monthly commit that starts to pay off if you sustain higher QPS or long-running sessions.
3) Private VPC / on-prem: recommended only if procurement/security require customer-managed networking and HSM integration. Higher setup time and separate support contract.

Open questions for us to finalize a tailored cost estimate (please answer by EOD Wed):
- Which percent of requests will be short (<=150 output tokens) vs long (>300 output tokens)? Rough split helps cost model.
- Any hard SLA beyond latencies mentioned (e.g., 99.9% uptime; penalty clauses)?
- Are you planning for multi-region failover or single-region US only?

Attachments: acme-cost-scenarios.xlsx (contains per-token vs reserved capacity worksheets), acme-procurement-checklist.pdf (procurement items + timelines).

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm token-length splits + procurement timeline.
- Us: run a short modeling workshop (30–45 minutes) with your infra and procurement next Thu to walk through the attached workbook and decide whether a 4-week reserved pilot makes sense.
- If procurement is ready to move, Aditya will send a preliminary commercial term sheet for a 4-week dedicated trial + conversion options.

Thanks — I can circulate a calendar invite for the modeling workshop once you confirm availability.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Thanks, Priya — helpful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Token split: we see ~70% short answers (<=150 tokens) and ~30% longer explanations (>=300 tokens) in our current beta logs.
- SLA: ops team wants 99.9% availability for production; pilot can accept 99.5%.
- Region: US-only to start; we may add EU later.

Procurement is okay with a short reserved pilot, but they need the attachable checklist completed and an estimate that shows the break-even point vs hosted. Can Aditya/Marissa help populate the workbook with the 70/30 split?

Samir

On Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 3:12 PM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Recap here so we have a shared starting point and clear asks for next week.

Thanks all — I'll take the 70/30 split and drop numbers into the workbook this afternoon. Initial observations:
- With Samir's split, hosted per-token costs for the pilot (30 days) look like ~$3.2k–$5.6k depending on model choice (cheaper family vs higher-quality) — see the "hosted" tab.
- Dedicated reserved: a minimal commit for a 4-week pilot that meets the latency SLO (we modeled conservative batching and KV cache disabled for correctness) is in the ballpark of $14k–$20k for the month, but gives predictable throughput and better 95p latency. The attached workbook contains a detailed monthly comparison and a sensitivity tab.
- Break-even: if you sustain >60% of the pilot volume after month 1, dedicated typically becomes more economical for the model family we discussed.

I'll mark cells with assumptions and add comments for the ops team. Marissa — can you join our modeling workshop to cover latency/throughput tradeoffs and pilot runbook?

Thanks,
Aditya
